text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.84% today after dropping sharply over the prior two trading days. The recovery comes as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East escalated—Saudi Arabia and Bahrain reported new attacks involving Iran-backed forces—which typically supports crude oil prices by raising supply concerns. US oil is trading at $89.53 per barrel, and the uptick in headlines about regional conflict may have eased some of the selling pressure the stock faced earlier in the week.

The stock had fallen 4.4% from November 13 to November 18, so today's modest gain appears to be a rebound rather than a new trend. Longer-term, the energy sector is hearing mixed signals: tighter gas markets in Europe from depleted winter storage and surging electricity demand from data centers could boost energy demand, but those tailwinds remain distant relative to the daily swings driven by oil price moves and near-term geopolitical risk.
